title: Expose automatic provider groups in the Mihomo dashboard
problem: The resilient profile keeps LIVE and SEED provider groups nested under PROVIDER-AUTO, but marking them hidden prevents Clash Party from listing them as separate groups with their provider-scoped nodes. Users cannot inspect or pin a node from either group in the dashboard.
outcome: Clash Party lists PROVIDER-AUTO, PROVIDER-AUTO-LIVE, and PROVIDER-AUTO-SEED. Opening each automatic group shows its real provider nodes with their original names, and the user can pin and unpin a node through the dashboard.

actors.name: Profile user
actors.responsibility: Inspect the LIVE or SEED nodes independently and use native pin/unpin controls.

actors.name: Service operator
actors.responsibility: Publish a profile whose group visibility and membership match the provider topology.

in_scope: Expose PROVIDER-AUTO-LIVE and PROVIDER-AUTO-SEED in the default Clash Party group list.
Keep LIVE and SEED node membership scoped to their respective providers and preserve original node names.
Keep both groups automatic url-test groups and support native fixed pinning followed by unpinning.
Preserve PROVIDER-AUTO fallback recovery, fetch routing, GLOBAL membership, and existing recovery behavior.
Add generated-profile regression coverage and verify the real dashboard flow when available.
out_of_scope: Changing the Clash Party application or its dashboard implementation.
Changing provider recovery or fetch routing to create UI workarounds.
Changing Cloudflare, DNS, Caddy, or unrelated production networking.

invariants.claim: PROVIDER-AUTO-LIVE and PROVIDER-AUTO-SEED are not hidden from the default dashboard group list.
invariants.enforcement: Renderer regression checks assert the groups do not set hidden=true; Mihomo API and dashboard observations verify visibility.

invariants.claim: LIVE remains a url-test group over only the LIVE provider, and SEED remains a url-test group over only the SEED provider, with original node names.
invariants.enforcement: Generated profile assertions and runtime API membership checks verify group types and node membership.

invariants.claim: Pinning temporarily fixes a selected node and unpinning restores automatic url-test selection for both groups.
invariants.enforcement: Mihomo runtime checks verify now/fixed transitions; the installed Clash Party dashboard acceptance flow verifies the actual UI controls.

invariants.claim: PROVIDER-AUTO fallback, PRIVATE/AUTO/BASE/PROXY/DIRECT structure, fetch routing, and GLOBAL remain free of individual provider nodes.
invariants.enforcement: Existing recovery tests and generated profile topology assertions remain unchanged and pass.

invariants.claim: Production-only credentials and profile data do not enter tracked source or artifacts.
invariants.enforcement: Artifacts and tests use neutral fixture names and values; review checks the complete diff.

failure_model.failure: The dashboard omits a group because it is marked hidden.
failure_model.response: Leave hidden unset for the two user-facing automatic provider groups and assert that property in regression tests.

failure_model.failure: A visible group does not resolve its provider nodes.
failure_model.response: Keep provider-scoped use references and reject acceptance unless the API and dashboard show the expected membership.

failure_model.failure: The dashboard displays a group but its pin/unpin controls do not preserve automatic behavior.
failure_model.response: Do not claim UI acceptance; verify the fixed state transition in the installed dashboard and Mihomo API.

acceptance_signals: Generated resilient profiles expose both groups without hidden=true, keep type url-test, and bind LIVE and SEED to their own providers.
Mihomo API returns each group with its real scoped nodes, now, and fixed fields; pinning sets fixed to the chosen node and unpinning clears it.
The installed Clash Party dashboard separately displays the LIVE and SEED groups and their original node names, and completes pin/unpin for both.
Existing recovery and fetch-routing regression/runtime checks pass without topology changes.
